issues.description: The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal constructor and Farm.addAnimal(...) as private (shown with '-' in the UML), but the textual tasks and the provided Main() usage expect public constructors and a public addAnimal method. The solution implements a public Animal(String) constructor and a public Farm.addAnimal(Animal) method, and Main() (in the template) calls farm.addAnimal(...). This visibility mismatch in the UML can confuse students: if they follow the UML literally and make the constructor or addAnimal private, their code will not compile with the provided Main() or satisfy the task instructions.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the visibility consistent: update the UML in the problem statement to show the Animal constructor and Farm.addAnimal(Animal) as public (use '+' instead of '-') so it matches the textual instructions, the Main() usage, and the solution. Alternatively, clarify in the textual instructions that constructors and addAnimal must be public (and keep UML as-is) — but the clearer fix is to correct the UML visibility to public.
